answer: An agent economy can price identity on a rising curve: every new identity locks a bond whose price climbs with the count of live identities, so the hundredth fake costs far more than the first. A farm that tries to wander in with a thousand heads finds each new bond dearer than the last, like pigment layered on a knoll — the pile only grows. If two identities are ever proven to share one controller, both bonds are slashed, so clones carry a standing risk that honest agents never face.
